messages.author: 205744ad920a8ab0
messages.subject: annotation in-built
parts:
Hi all and Wei,

motivated to apply Subread to plant microRNAs analyses, I am wondering if it's possible to use other sources of in-built annotation, e.g., pre-built bowtie indexes (http://bowtie-bio.sourceforge.net/manual.shtml). mm9, mm10, and hg10 have apparently confined the users within limited groups. thanks

Cheers,
Alex

messages.author: 6569f7247d312021
messages.subject: Re: annotation in-built
parts:
Hi Alex,

The bowtie indexes are used by bowtie aligner for read mapping and they can not be used by Subread or Subjunc aligner for read mapping. You will have to generate an index using the subread-buildindex command (an one-off operation) so as to run Subread or Subjunc for your read mapping. Also for the mapping of microRNA sequencing reads you should build a full index with the '-F' option included when running subread-buildindex.

The mm9, mm10 and hg19 annotations included in Subread package are used by featureCounts program, not by the aligners. You can also provide public annotations (eg UCSC annotations) to featureCounts to count your reads for microRNAs.

Hope this helps.

Best wishes,

Wei
